title: Hazel and the Safehouse
premise: Kestrel Quintana, a financial-crimes investigator who has spent years laundering her own past into respectability, is pulled back into the covert world she fled when the safehouse she once ran is listed for sale online — its interior photographed, its secrets exposed. The listing is a message from an old handler: extract Nadia Volkova, a defector carrying evidence that could destroy the syndicate Kestrel's former employer protects. But every clue suggests Nadia is bait in a trap designed to flush out Kestrel herself. As loyalty to her old network collides with the truth about what they did to her family, and as her growing bond with Nadia deepens into something neither expected, Kestrel must choose between duty to the people who made her and love for the woman she was sent to betray. In the end, Kestrel burns her own legend — leaking the syndicate's ledger and faking both their deaths — so that she and Nadia can finally belong somewhere unlisted.
about_author: Marguerite Lockridge is the pen name of a former compliance analyst who spent a decade tracing money through shell companies before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about people whose clean lives are built on dirty ledgers, and she still keeps a go-bag packed out of habit.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Scrolling real estate listings at 2 a.m., Kestrel freezes on a familiar floor plan: the safehouse, staged for sale, down to the hidden panel behind the bookshelf visible in photo seven. Someone is selling her old life. Emotional beat: cold dread beneath a polished surface.

chapters.title: Clean Money
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. At work she closes another immaculate case, praised by superiors who don't know her history. Her go-bag sits in the closet like a confession. A burner phone she kept 'for sentiment' buzzes once. Emotional beat: the suffocation of a life built on denial.

chapters.title: The Handler's Voice
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. The call comes from Marek, her old handler: the listing was deliberate, a summons. Nadia Volkova, a syndicate accountant turned defector, is holed up in Riga with a ledger that names names — including people who destroyed Kestrel's family. Extract her in nine days. Emotional beat: the pull of unfinished business.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Costs
chapters.summary: Marek's POV. Marek briefs his actual employer, revealing Nadia may be expendable — the extraction is really about recovering the ledger and identifying who leaked the safehouse photos. He justifies using Kestrel as both asset and decoy. Emotional beat: institutional cynicism wearing a loyal face.

chapters.title: Nine Days
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. She lies to her partner Dana about a conference, packs the go-bag, and studies Nadia's file — noticing the defector requested her by name. That detail itches like a splinter. Emotional beat: guilt sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Riga Rain
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Arriving under a false passport, Kestrel makes contact through a bookstore dead-drop and finds the city crawling with watchers. Her first surveillance pass confirms someone else is hunting Nadia too — professionals, not police. Emotional beat: hunter realizing she's also prey.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Asked for Me
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. In a safe flat above a shuttered bakery, Nadia counts her remaining hours and rehearses her pitch. She knows exactly who Kestrel Quintana is — and what was done to her family — because she helped hide the paper trail years ago. Emotional beat: fear braided with hope.

chapters.title: Contact
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Kestrel breaches the flat; Nadia doesn't run. Instead she says Kestrel's real childhood name aloud. The extraction becomes a negotiation conducted at gunpoint over cold tea. Emotional beat: recognition that changes everything.

chapters.title: Terms of Extraction
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Nadia offers the ledger in exchange for the truth about Operation Larkspur — the op that killed Kestrel's brother. Kestrel refuses to believe her own side was responsible, but the doubt takes root. They agree to move at dawn. Emotional beat: loyalty beginning to crack.

chapters.title: The Bookstore Burns
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Their first move is ambushed; the bookstore contact is killed and the flat torched. Kestrel realizes the ambush used her own tradecraft signatures — someone inside her old network sold them. Emotional beat: betrayal as physical wound.

chapters.title: Running on Rails
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. On a night train toward the coast, Nadia patches Kestrel's grazed shoulder and tells her how the syndicate launders money through art auctions — and how Marek signed off on one of the transfers. Kestrel calls him anyway; his answers are too smooth. Emotional beat: intimacy forged in motion.

chapters.title: Dana Calls
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. From a ferry terminal, Kestrel takes a risky call home. Dana isn't angry — she's frightened, saying two men asked about Kestrel at the office. Kestrel realizes her cover life is compromised too. Emotional beat: the two lives collapsing into one.

chapters.title: The Auction House
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Following the money trail, they infiltrate a Vienna preview where the syndicate parks its profits. Kestrel photographs the ledger's corroborating records while Nadia works the room like she owns it. Emotional beat: competence as seduction; the trap tightening.

chapters.title: Bait Confirmed
chapters.summary: Marek's POV. Marek learns Kestrel has gone off-script and orders the Vienna team to let her run — she'll lead them to whoever leaked the photos. He tells himself he's protecting her. Emotional beat: self-deception curdling into something darker.

chapters.title: Confession on the Danube
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. On a night boat, Nadia admits she didn't defect for ideals alone — she defected because she couldn't carry Larkspur's paperwork anymore, and she chose Kestrel because Kestrel deserved the truth. Kestrel, furious and undone, almost walks. Emotional beat: love arriving disguised as anger.

chapters.title: The Leak Is Me
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Reconstructing the timeline, Kestrel discovers the safehouse photos were posted by her brother's old partner — alive, hidden, trying to lure the syndicate into the open using her as the hook. Everyone she trusted has been steering her. Emotional beat: grief reorganizing into purpose.

chapters.title: Counteroffer
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Kestrel contacts Marek directly and offers a trade: the ledger for Larkspur's sealed files. He agrees to meet in Prague — and she knows he'll bring shooters. She and Nadia plan the exchange knowing it's a trap they intend to spring backward. Emotional beat: resolve replacing fear.

chapters.title: Prague Exchange
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. In a riverfront warehouse, the handoff detonates into violence. Marek confesses Larkspur was sanctioned from the top — then tries to take Nadia and burn the ledger. Kestrel chooses, openly, for the first time in her life. Emotional beat: the climax of loyalty vs. truth.

chapters.title: Ash and Ledger
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. Wounded, they escape with copies of everything and torch the originals' transport. Marek is left for his employers to answer for. Nadia realizes Kestrel burned her legend to save her — no handler, no cover, no way back. Emotional beat: terror and tenderness in the same breath.

chapters.title: Dead on Paper
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. With her brother's partner's help, they stage their deaths — a car off a coastal road, dental records, a tidy fire. Kestrel sends the full ledger to three journalists and one prosecutor, timed to publish after the funerals. Emotional beat: liberation that feels like mourning.

chapters.title: Unlisted
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. Weeks later, in a rented cottage far from any map, the news breaks: arrests, resignations, a senator's career ending mid-sentence. Nadia watches Kestrel sleep and understands she was never bait — she was the reason someone finally told the truth. Emotional beat: belonging without conditions.

chapters.title: Hazel and the Safehouse
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Epilogue. Kestrel plants hazel saplings where the safehouse stood, now sold to strangers who will never know what happened there. Her go-bag stays packed — but by the door, not hidden, and half of it belongs to Nadia. Emotional beat: peace chosen daily, not granted.
